topic.name: The Axis of Symmetry of a Parabola

question.text: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=kx^2+3x-15$ is $x=4.$ Find the value of $k.$
question.explanation:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, we will set our result equal to $4.$

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=k$ and $b=3$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

\begin{align*} x &= -\dfrac{3}{2(k)}\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{3}{2k}. \end{align*}

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=4,$ so we must have

\begin{align*} -\dfrac{3}{2k} &= 4 \\[5pt] -3 &= 8k \\[5pt] k &= -\dfrac{3}{8}. \end{align*}

question.text: Find the axis of symmetry for the parabola $y=4x^2-16x+5.$
question.explanation:
The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

We substitute $a=4$ and $b=-16$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry. This gives \begin{align*} x &= -\dfrac{(-16)}{2(4)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{16}{8}\\[5pt] &= 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=2.$

question.text: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y = -4x^2 - 20x - 15?$
question.explanation:
The parabola's vertex lies on the symmetry axis, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ is given by \[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a = -4$ and $b = -20$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get \begin{align*} x & = -\dfrac{(-20)}{2(-4)}\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{(-20)}{(-8)}\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{5}{2}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x = -\dfrac{5}{2}.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x = -\dfrac{5}{2}$ into the original equation: \begin{align*} y &= -4x^2 - 20x - 15\\[5pt] & = -4\left(-\dfrac{5}{2}\right)^2 - 20\left(-\dfrac{5}{2}\right) - 15\\[5pt] & = -25 + 50 - 15\\[5pt] &= 10 \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is at $\left(\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ -\dfrac{5}{2}}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{10}\right).$

question.text: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y = -6x^2 + 36x - 50?$
question.explanation:
The parabola's vertex lies on the symmetry axis, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ is given by \[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a = -6$ and $b = 36$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get \begin{align*} x & = -\dfrac{36}{2(-6)}\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{36}{(-12)}\\[5pt] &= 3. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x = 3.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x = 3$ into the original equation: \begin{align*} y &= -6x^2 + 36x - 50\\[5pt] & = -6(3)^2 + 36(3) - 50\\[5pt] & = -54 + 108 - 50\\[5pt] &= 4 \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is at $\Big(\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 3}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4}\Big).$

question.text: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y = 2x^2 + kx - 5$ is $x = \dfrac32.$ Determine the value of $k.$
question.explanation:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, we will set our result equal to $\dfrac32.$

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ is given by \[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a = 2$ and $b = k$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get \begin{align*} x & = -\dfrac{k}{2(2)}\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{k}{4}. \end{align*}

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x = \dfrac32,$ so we must have \begin{align*} -\dfrac{k}4 &= \dfrac32 \\[5pt] -2k & = 12 \\[5pt] k & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-6}. \end{align*}
